summary: BBN's host status report for February 28 to March 10, 1972, noting the ETAC Terminal IMP was installed in the period. It was updated by RFC 326.

plainLanguage.summary: This report lists host predictions and daily connection-test results for part of March 1972. It explains which hosts were left out of testing and what each test code means.

subtitle: A BBN report on ARPANET host tests from February 28 to March 10, 1972.

tldr.problem: Network users needed information about which hosts were available and which were not being tested as servers.
tldr.mechanism: The report combines host status predictions with connection-test results recorded by date and time.
tldr.outcome: The ETAC Terminal IMP was installed during this period. RFC 319 obsoletes RFC 315 and was updated by RFC 326.

today: RFC 319 is listed as Unknown. It obsoletes RFC 315 and was updated by RFC 326.

sections.title: What the Report Covers
sections.content:
Ellen Westheimer reports on most Network Hosts from February 28 to March 10. The ETAC Terminal IMP, Network Address 148, was installed during this period.

The report excludes hosts not expected to operate regularly as servers and hosts intended only as users. The latter group includes the Terminal IMPs, the Network Control Center computer used to collect statistics, and several listed site computers.
sections.plainLanguage: The report covers host tests from late February through March 10. It also records the installation of the ETAC Terminal IMP.

sections.title: Host Status and Predictions
sections.content:
A table lists each host's network address, site, computer, status or prediction, and the person who supplied that information. Entries include server, user-only, and planned availability descriptions. A note says that the UCLA NMC would like users to arrange access in advance.

The UCLA IBM-360/91 offered a Network Job Service (NETRJS), which the BBN Terminal IMP could not test. The report assumed that a successful initial connection to the NETRJS logger indicated that the service was functioning.
sections.plainLanguage: One table reports what each site said about its host, including whether it served others or was still expected to become available.

sections.title: Daily Connection-Test Results
sections.content:
The test table records results from the BBN Terminal IMP at specified Eastern times. Its codes show whether a host was open and accessible, dead or inaccessible, briefly open, refused the connection, or timed out. A timeout means the host failed to complete the Initial Connection Protocol and open a connection within 60 seconds.

A hash mark indicates that a site had warned it might not be available at that time. The tables therefore distinguish test failures from times when a site had already announced limited availability.
sections.plainLanguage: The tables record the outcome of each test. A hash mark warns that the site had said it might be unavailable.

items.label: Dead
items.desc: Host was dead or inaccessible from the BBN Terminal IMP.

items.label: Half open
items.desc: Host opened a connection, then closed it or stopped responding.

items.label: Open
items.desc: Host opened a connection and was accessible to users.

items.label: Refused
items.desc: Host returned a CLS to the initial RFC.

items.label: Timed out
items.desc: Host did not complete the ICP and open a connection within 60 seconds.

references.text: RFC 315, the earlier host status report obsoleted by this RFC.
